A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NID framework despite the changed title and expanded evaluation. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original NID experiments on node classification, graph classification, clustering, link prediction, efficiency, and molecular linear probing, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds clustering evaluations, additional model integrations, design ablations, inductive node classification, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The per-layer RVQ procedure, joint graph-learning and quantization loss, and downstream readouts remain. v2 extends the framework's concrete learning objectives through DGCluster and AutoGCL; its clustering application replaces GraphMAE plus k-means with DGCluster-based learning and clustering. These are limited procedural extensions of the existing framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds Questions for node classification, expands clustering from Cora and CiteSeer to seven datasets, and adds inductive node classification on ogbn-products. Conversely, ogbl-ppa link prediction is removed. The seven MoleculeNet evaluations are retained in Appendix D.2 rather than newly added.

E2.justification: The clustering comparator set is substantially replaced with methods including DGCluster, DMoN, NOCD, and SDCN. Main node-classification comparisons add Graph-MLP and VQGraph while removing numerous previous comparators. TUDataset comparisons add AutoGCL, AD-GCL, MVGRL, and GraphMAE and remove graph2vec. SAGE disappears from link-prediction comparisons and GatedGCN from LRGB comparisons.

E3.justification: Clustering adopts DGCluster's protocol and reports NMI/F1 instead of the previous accuracy/NMI/macro-F1 combination. Reported model configurations also change: ogbn-arxiv moves from a seven-layer GAT trained for 2,000 epochs to a five-layer SAGE trained for 1,000 epochs, and several hidden dimensions increase. New inductive and ablation experiments introduce additional evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: v2 adds VQGraph reconstruction-loss removal experiments, end-to-end versus post-hoc RVQ comparisons, codebook-size comparisons, and inductive versus transductive evaluation in Tables 14 and 16–18. Earlier codebook-usage, retrieval, qualitative, and K/M/L analyses remain. The training-ratio analysis is redrawn and loses its CiteSeer series.

E5.justification: The five-seed graph-classification and ten-run mean/standard-deviation reporting policies remain. A limited addition is uncertainty accompanying VQGraph's ogbn-products score: v1 Table 9 gives 79.17 alone, whereas v2 Tables 16 and 18 give 79.17 ± 0.21. This does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive clustering, Questions, AutoGCL, inductive, efficiency, and ablation results. Existing comparator scores also change: GCN's Peptides-func AP rises from a reported 0.5930 to 0.6762, reversing its ranking against the unchanged NID value of 0.6608. The main ogbn-arxiv NID entry changes from 71.27 to 70.52 alongside a backbone change, so it is not a same-setting deterioration. Molecular linear-probing results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 introduces Section 3.3, Theorem 1, and its Appendix B proof, absent from v1. The analysis assumes a simplified one-layer GCN, orthogonal class patterns, and aligned weights, and claims class-distinct IDs and zero classification error after training a linear head. This substantially expands the formal mathematical content.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims compact, interpretable graph representations with competitive performance and faster inference. v2 additionally presents theoretical validation as a contribution and claims that integrating NID can improve its underlying GNNs, uncover hidden patterns, and reveal substantial redundancy in GNN embeddings. These additions materially broaden the stated contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier global-information explanation for heterophilic performance with discussion of information preservation and hidden patterns, particularly on imbalanced Questions. New appendix discussions justify excluding reconstruction loss, favor joint over post-hoc training, explain inductive applicability, and interpret training overhead. The explicit limitations concerning very large datasets and future LLM applications are retained.

D1.justification: v2 revises and expands dataset-specific hyperparameters and adds RVQ optimization explanations, codebook-size accounting, and pretraining timings of 5.9 versus 5.8 seconds per epoch. The abstract changes code availability from 'is available' to 'will be made available.' Documentation also becomes inconsistent: Table 12 lists GCN for unsupervised node classification while Section 4.1.2 still specifies GAT.

R1.justification: v2 incorporates substantial new literature on clustering, AutoGCL, quantization, and theoretical analysis. It grounds revised node-classification comparisons in Luo et al.'s work on strong classical GNN baselines and expands its positioning against VQGraph. These substantive changes extend beyond the switch from numbered to author-year citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements, related-work discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Evaluation is reorganized to lead with supervised learning, with a new overall-performance subsection. Appendices are reorganized around the added proof, experiments, and discussion, and terminology shifts toward compact discrete representations.

P2.justification: v2 merges the homophilic and heterophilic classification tables, introduces separate backbone/NID rows, adds timing and storage rows, replaces the clustering display, and adds several appendix tables. The training-ratio figure moves into the main text and changes from three panels to an overlaid two-series plot, apparently reversing the earlier Cora/PubMed labels. Page styling and table formatting also change substantially.

improvement.justification: Matched GNN comparisons, broader clustering evaluation, targeted ablations in Tables 16–17, and new efficiency and inductive results strengthen the empirical assessment beyond v1. However, v2 introduces conflicting backbone descriptions and an inconsistent RVQ residual formula in Appendix E.1, while changing its code-release statement to future availability. The added theory concerns an idealized setting. The empirical gains support a net improvement, but these documentation and reproducibility weaknesses limit its overall magnitude.
